utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. The affirmation you made to tell the truth still applies. If you could sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what the security situation was like in the territory of the Urosevac SUP towards the end of 1998 and the beginning of 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The security situation in the territory of the SUP of Urosevac at the end of 1998 and the beginning of 1999 was exceptionally complex and exceptionally difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How come it was so complex?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was reflected in the fact that attacks were intensified against members of the army and police and that more and more people of all ethnic backgrounds were being kidnapped. Also, Albanian terrorists had consolidated their ranks; and their strongholds, bunkers, et cetera, became even stronger. They intensified their training in Albania, all of our intelligence pointed to that. Also, they brought in weapons illegally from the territory of Albania. So the situation was very difficult in that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have on our screens D133.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tab 30 in your binder. Witness, what is this document and who was it sent to?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a report sent to the MUP staff for Kosovo and Metohija, and it is sent to Colonel Mijatovic, Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The date is the 18th of November, 1998. Could you please tell me who signed the document?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the date, and I signed the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It says here for the chief of the secretariat?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please give me your comment with regard to the first paragraph of this document.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has to do with something that happened on the 17th of November, 1998. Mr. Sali Emini, from the village of Racak, came to report a case. The ten uniformed members of the so-called KLA had come to the village of Racak and ordered the locals to leave the village because a greater number of them wanted to move into it. The uniformed members of the so-called KLA came to the village at about 1100 hours and the locals immediately moved out of the village in large numbers at about 1600 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Since this was on the 15th and the rest on the 17th, did you check this out? Please look at paragraph 3 as well, I'd like to hear your comment.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After receiving this information and when the citizen complained about the problems they were facing in the village, the chief secretariat sent a patrol, a large one, to the village of Racak.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So was that information confirmed, that the KLA was present in Racak?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, there had been a terrorist attack, and I have an excellent recollection of what happened. The vehicle was damaged, and the policemen were not seriously wounded. Lecic, their commander, was with them too. It was only the vehicle that was damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D008-5606, could we have that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tab 31 in your binder. This is a document dated the 27th of December, 1998. It's from the OKP. Did you receive information about such documents and their content?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of this document. I see that it was submitted by Jasovic, Dragan Jasovic and Momcilo Sparavalo. On the basis of all the knowledge that they had and on the basis of the notes written up by the policemen and that we forward to them, so on the basis of all that information, they wrote this up. And the chief of SUP briefed us about this at the regular morning meeting. He made us aware of all the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would just be interested in the last paragraph on page 1, if you can see it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Intelligence indicates that every day members of the so-called KLA from the villages of Kosare, municipality of Urosevac -- sorry, actually, Jezerce, Malopoljce, and Petrovo come to Dramnjak and to Kosare to launch terrorist attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where is Kosare? On which road?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village of Kosare is on the road between Urosevac and Stimlje, roughly around the middle of that road. Slivovo and Kosare are very close to one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You had an observation post in Crnoljevo; on which road is that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are observation posts in Crnoljevo on the Stimlje-Suva Reka-Prizren section of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This intelligence that you received about Kosare, when did that actually become a topical matter?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The situation regarding Kosare was such that the police were attacked. I can't remember the exact date. I think it was mid-January. A policemen --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we'll get to that. But this is the 27th of December, 1998, the document that we are looking at now.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please repeat your question again?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It says here in this document that there are more and more attacks against Kosare and Slivovo and you explained to us which road that is, however, since when had such things been noticed, that is to say, KLA attacks?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my understanding, there was already information by the time this document was written. So in that period the situation became increasingly complicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is that the period when the KVM was present?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have D138. And could this document please be admitted into evidence. Could we just have a look at the end of the document, please. Could the document please be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00827.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D138. Page 2 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It is tab 32 in your binder. This is a criminal report about something that happened on the 10th of January, 1999, OKP Urosevac. Can you just tell us what you know about what happened on the 10th of January, 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mentioned it a moment ago, and I know what the date is. The 10th of January, in the morning, Nenad Mitrovic, deputy commander, policemen Svetislav Przic and Miroslav Zivic, as far as I can remember. Yes, yes, here he is. They set out from Stimlje to Urosevac. And in the area of the village of Slivovo - Slivovo and Kosare are nearby - they were fired at from automatic weapons from the Muslim cemetery. That is to say that the terrorists were within the Muslim cemetery and opened fire from there and seriously wounded Svetislav Przic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have D139.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tab 33. This is a report on contact with members of the OSCE Mission. The date is the 10th of January, 1999, SUP Urosevac. Did you receive this report?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This report was written by Lieutenant Sasa Draskovic. I received that report and sent it to the analysis people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether the KVM verified this event and whether they did something about it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the OSCE Mission registered this event, however, they did nothing on account of it. They didn't help me at all -- they didn't help us at all with regard to throwing more light on what happened.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the number please be repeated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D009-0931.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It is tab 34 in your binder. This is a survey of activities in the Urosevac SUP dated the 12th of January, 1999. Could you please tell us who it was sent to?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This survey on developments and activities was sent to the MUP staff for Kosovo-Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I see that someone signed on behalf of the chief, was it maybe you?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I think that this is the signature of Branko Debeljkovic, head of the crime police department.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm interested in the third paragraph of this report. Was that one of the things that members of your police department were supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, you are asking me about paragraph 3?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Concerning information --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes. This is police work. Persons were brought in to be interviewed. So members of the police, they bring in persons, they write up a report, and they hand them over to OKP employees for further processing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And in the one but last paragraph, we see the answer of the person who talked to the verifiers?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So between the 10th and 12th, what was it that the representative of the police told the verifiers?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The member -- or rather, the representative of the police told the verifiers that the persons who had been brought in were released after they were interviewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever receive any report from the verifiers, from the sites where they went to verify particular matters?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never in writing. Perhaps they explained a few things orally.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00828.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: After all these events from November until mid-January, that is, from mid-November 1998 until mid-January 1999, did the SUP of Urosevac take any action with regard to countering the activity of the terrorist groups in the territory?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Urosevac SUP, that is, the chief of the secretariat, based on all facts and circumstances, including the operative intelligence that we had at the time, compiled a proposal to the MUP staff for Kosovo and Metohija to arrest terrorists, the terrorists who had committed the crimes I mentioned. The wounding of Przic, the kidnapping of other persons, et cetera. As we had intelligence to the effect that they were -- they were in -- around the villages of Racak, Petrovac, and Malopoljce, the secretariat drafted a proposal. The content of the proposal was to make a security assessment, to put everything on paper, and everything was forwarded to the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know how the staff reacted to that proposal?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on that proposal of the chief of the secretariat, the staff made a plan to apprehend the terrorist group that had committed the crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know who took part in the apprehension of terrorists in the village of Racak?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. For the simple fact that, as far as I know, one day before the operation was launched, we had a briefing with the chief of the secretariat in his office. He briefed us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who was present and what he briefed you about?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was the chief who chaired the meeting, the chief of the secretariat that is. Then there was Goran Radosavljevic, aka Guri; I was there; Milan Lecic; and Jelic, Krzman Jelic, the commander of the the barracks of the 143rd [as interpreted] Intervention Brigade was invited to join us later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what did the chief say at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief didn't explain the plan to us, he didn't acquaint us with it; he just told us briefly that the arrest would be carried out on the 15th. But he didn't mention any details of the plan. He merely said that the operation would be led by Goran Radosavljevic whose nickname was Guri. I believe that he was a major at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what about Colonel Jelic, he was also at the meeting. Did he take part in the the discussion, and was there anything special with regard to his presence?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Jelic was present at the meeting, but he didn't comment. He just received information for the sake of his men to avoid unwanted consequences in the field. He was the commander of the territorial unit, and it was desirable that he be informed of the activities of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As far as you know, did the military participate in the arrest of the terrorists?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was a classical police operation, the -- I mean, the apprehension of the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you in Racak when the operation was carried out?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't there. I was at Stimlje. On the 14th, at that meeting, the chief of the secretariat gave me instructions to be ready on the following morning at 6.00. I remember the hour, it was 6.00 a.m. And the two of us were supposed to go to Stimlje.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So did you meet up with him? Did you go to Stimlje?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We met at that time. And after 10 or 15 minutes having picked up our personal things, we set out for Stimlje.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was the passage to Stimlje safe?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The passage was not safe. The traffic police had set up a check-point in the area of Kosare, and during the operation they didn't allow vehicles to pass.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And did you pass though?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that we did. When the chief of the SUP overtook some vehicles and we reached the traffic police control, they told him, Chief, we have orders to block any passage until further notice. And he replied, Yes, it is blocked for everybody else but not for me. And then they saluted him and we moved on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You say that you went to Stimlje. Where exactly in Stimlje?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went right to the police station in Stimlje.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What did you do at the police station, where were you, what took place there?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the police station in Stimlje, I can't quite remember how long we stayed there, but we left Urosevac around 6.15, 6.20. We took some time to get to Stimlje. And we went to the office of the commander of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was the commander present?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The commander with a company of active-duty and reserve policemen had to go to Crnoljevo and change shifts because there was a check-point for securing the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did anybody receive you at the Stimlje police station?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I remember, there was assistant commander Zoran Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where is the office of the commander of the Stimlje police station?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The office of the commander is upstairs. So you climb the stairs, go right, you walk through the office of the deputy commander and the assistant commander, and then you turn left and enter the commander's office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before my friend goes on, I see where he is leading to and I think the time -- well, it's hard to find an appropriate time, but I have to place on record the objection of the Prosecution in respect to leading evidence about the events that occurred in the office of the command of the Stimlje police station from this witness for the simple reason that it is not mentioned in the 65 ter summary for the witness, yet it is one of the live issues in the case, and a matter which ought to have been addressed. This issue was not mentioned in the 65 ter summary of the previous witness, and I did not object to it being led. But upon advisement, I have been advised that the Prosecution ought to put on record its objection to the leading of important evidence on controversial matters that are specifically alleged in the the indictment and the pre-trial brief when it is not placed in the 65 ter summary of the witness. I did not object to the previous one because although the Prosecution was prejudiced, we were able to deal with it. The situation is similar in this case, there is prejudice, but I think we can deal with it and therefore I ask for no sanction. But I have been advised that it is proper that I place it on record that leading this evidence is contrary to the rules and is also flouting the orders of the Court made in October or November last year. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I know that in the summary for this witness it was stated that he would give evidence about the events in Racak and about his knowledge concerning that. The topic was tackled by the Prosecution first. The Prosecution put forward evidence about this and therefore the Defence decided to have witnesses give evidence about this too. For this witness, it was stated that he would give evidence about the events in Racak because he was there and we will hear what he knows now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The point at the moment is that you are dealing with events at Stimlje. They may be connected to Racak, but there is no indication in the summary that the witness will deal with events in Stimlje and there has apparently been no additional notice to that contained in the Rule 65 ter notice. So that's the point that you should comment on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness will tell us how he got information about Racak. He is telling us where he was, what he did, and how he got the information. It is not my understanding that the pre-trial brief should include all facts about which the witness would give evidence. We didn't have witness statements yet, but we gave a broader framework of the contents of their evidence instead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The rule requires that you give a summary of the facts on which each witness will testify.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We considered that his knowledge about Racak is the framework, and that is included in the summary rather than exactly what he knew and how he found out and the like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Your position is that you considered you were complying with the rules by the summary that's been given, is that what you're saying? I have to make it clear again as I hope I made it clear yesterday, we do not agree. The summary avoids summarising the evidence of the witness about this material event and perhaps others. As I commented yesterday, if this is an isolated matter, we can more readily overlook it, but if it becomes a pattern, we will not be able to. Remedies available to the Chamber include, at the least, allowing the Prosecution a delay to prepare to deal in cross-examination with the matter, and that will often mean that the witness has to wait here in The Hague. But more significantly, depending on the seriousness of the matter, we can refuse to hear the evidence at all. Now, you can thank at the moment Mr. Stamp for making it clear that on this occasion the Prosecution can overcome the problem because we are reaching the point with the summaries, as I put to Mr. Popovic yesterday, that there is almost an apparent pattern of avoidance of the material evidence of the witness in what is provided under Rule 65 ter. I did yesterday say to Mr. Popovic that there should -- when I say yesterday, it may have been the day before - I made it clear that your summaries should be reviewed. And if there are matters that are material in the case which are not adequately summarised, supplementary notice to the Prosecution should be given immediately so that we don't constantly encounter this problem. Because of the position taken by Mr. Stamp, carry on, but be very firmly on notice, Mr. Djurdjic, that we are concerned that there has been a significant failure in these Rule 65 ter notices to give the Prosecution notice of material facts that will be led from the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. If we notice that the summaries of future witnesses are not in line with your instructions, we will submit more detailed summaries of the evidence of the witnesses to be called in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you went to the office of the station commander, you and the chief of the SUP did. Can you tell us what your activities were while you were at the Stimlje police station?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the way it was: I and the chief of the secretariat were there. He had radio communications by which he followed what was happening in Racak, and from time to time he reported to the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you establish contact with the units that were carrying out the operation in Racak, or could you communicate with the staff?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not have such communication. I had the regular communication. I always had the regular channels by which I could monitor the activities of police stations in the territory of the secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During the day, can you tell me how the situation developed to the best of your knowledge concerning the operation in Racak and how you learned about that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the fact that the police station of Stimlje is not very far away from Racak, it's a few kilometres away, say up to 3 kilometres away as the crow flies, perhaps not even that far away as the crow flies, from the point when we arrived we heard sporadic gun-fire, and later on it became more and more intensive, and there was fighting practically all day long.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, as you were learning about this, did you hear of casualties during the fighting?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no detailed information. There was information from time to time to the effect that there was fighting and that there were fatalities. That is what I heard via the radio transmitter that the SUP chief had.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Once you had this information, were any measures taken?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in view of the situation and in view of the fact that there were fatalities, the SUP chief instructed me to inform the SUP duty service to establish an on-site investigation team. That is to say, to make the investigative judge, the public prosecutor, and the crime technicians aware of what was happening, namely, that they should be prepared and that they should go to Stimlje in order to carry out an investigation on site.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The crime technicians, did they arrive in Stimlje during the course of the day?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that with any certainty, but I think that the team, the forensic team, did arrive during the course of the morning at the premises of the duty service of the police station or the buildings right next door. That is to say, in the same compound there are other buildings and offices, and I think that they sat there and waited.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: How did the situation develop further while you were at the Stimlje police station?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, we were following the situation up until the afternoon. Fighting went on practically until night-time. It was in January, and night falls early in our part of the world. I remember that at one point in time, Goran Radosavljevic decided that the OPG that he headed withdraw from the place where the blockade was. As far as I know and from what I heard from the chief, they were above Racak when they withdrew, and the reason why they withdrew was that there were fierce attacks coming from all sides. So it was quite impossible for the PJP company from Urosevac to remain in that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that you informed the Urosevac SUP that they should inform the investigating judge and the team that they should come to Stimlje. Did the team come; and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that investigating judge Danica Marinkovic was there and to the best of my recollection, Mr. Ismet Sufta was there too, he was either the public prosecutor or the deputy district public prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where was it that they arrived in Stimlje, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came to the commander's office; that's where they were in contact with the chief of the secretariat. And the chief of the secretariat, after that, told them at one moment, that is to say, before the forces withdrew, while it was still more peaceful, that conditions had been created for them to go and carry out an on-site investigation, that is to say, the investigating judge and the public prosecutor along with the team.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The investigating judge and the deputy district public prosecutor, did they actually go to carry out an investigation in Racak?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they set out. I didn't leave my office actually. I know that they went there and we heard via radio that an attack had been launched and that it wasn't safe for them even to start the on-site investigation, so they had to return yet again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether the investigating judge and the team were in Racak, and was it from Racak that they returned under these circumstances when the KLA attacked, as you told us?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They had already entered Racak, but there was strong gun-fire and therefore they could not stay there. So the investigating judge decided to go back, and once conditions were created again, the on-site investigation could be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether any weapons were found in the village of Racak while the investigating judge and the team were there?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm exactly whether it was at that time when the Judge was there, but I know that part of the weapons were brought to the police station in Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know which weapons were brought on the 15th of January in the Urosevac SUP?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure exactly. But as far as I can remember, a 12.7 millimetre Browning. I know that was found for sure. Then a 7.9 millimetre submachine-gun and several rifles. Believe me, I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How long did you stay in Stimlje on the 15th of January, 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stayed until dusk roughly, but by then we found out that in Kosare, in the area of Kosare, the army and the police were attacked again, or, rather, innocent citizens who were passing down that road too. The chief, his driver, and I drove around that road and then we went via Lipljan to Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 16th and 17th of January, did you have any information as to what was going on in Racak, and where were you?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 16th and 17th I was not in Stimlje. I stayed at my own place of work in Urosevac, but I remember that yet again an attempt was made to carry out the on-site investigation. During those days, those two days, it was impossible to enter Racak because the Albanian terrorists opened gun-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what happened afterwards at the Urosevac SUP?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. On what day?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You said that on the 16th and 17th you were not at the Urosevac SUP and that the on-site investigation could not be carried out to the best of your knowledge, and I'm asking you what happened next at the Urosevac SUP to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know is that the team went in order to carry out an on-site investigation, but they didn't manage to do it. However, Mr. Walker pointed out in the media in advance that what had happened was a massacre, and great attention was being devoted to that problem by the state leadership, with the very top leadership, and all of us, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge on the 16th and 17th to the effect that there had been a massacre in Racak?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no massacre whatsoever. Our knowledge was as follows: There was fighting going on and there were fatalities. To the best of our knowledge it was terrorists who got killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know what the further activities were, how things developed after that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of the details. What I remember is that an attempt was made to carry out an on-site investigation and that that did not succeed either on the 16th or the 17th. Believe me, I don't remember any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So what was done about it in view of the fact that on-site investigations could not be carried out during those two days?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since it was impossible to carry out an on-site investigation, the chief of the secretariat - I don't remember who else was there in addition to myself. Actually, I think that Branislav Debeljkovic was there too, but I can't remember. He was the head of the crime police department. And we were informed that the staff planned to carry out a de-blockade, or rather, to make it possible to create conditions to carry out an on-site investigation in Racak and that on the following day an action would be conducted with regard to that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know when the de-blockade of Racak was carried out?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was in the morning hours. I cannot confirm this exactly. I know that the PJP company from Urosevac took part in all of that. Now, whether the OPG was there or some other company of the PJP, I really cannot say. However, it started in the morning. Once again, I went to Stimlje with the chief of SUP on the 18th, sometime in the morning. I cannot be very specific, but I think it was around 8.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So what happened? Where were you at the police station?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the police station yet again we were in the office of the commander of the police station. That is where we followed how the situation developed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how the situation developed while you were there at the Stimlje police station?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is how the situation developed on that day: Sporadic gun-fire was heard, that is to say, there was fighting going on up until midday approximately. I wouldn't know the exact time. But I know that control was supposed to be established over Racak. I know that Danica Marinkovic, the investigative judge, came; then Dragomir Zivic, the deputy district public prosecutor; and I think that Sasa Dobricanin was there, pathologist -- or I don't know exactly what his function is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This on-site investigation team, or rather, the investigating judge came to carry out an on-site investigation in Racak. Did the on-site investigation actually take place? If so, when, and what happened?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They arrived around midday, I remember that very well. The chief and I were in the office. And the team then talked to the chief, and the chief explained that conditions had not been created yet for them to go out to carry out the on-site investigation. While we were sitting in the office say for 10 or 15 or 20 minutes, I cannot be more specific than that, General Djordjevic came at that moment and he was there in the office with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened then?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, the chief of the secretariat briefly informed General Djordjevic about the situation concerning the de-blockade of Racak, or rather, creating conditions for the on-site investigation. Again, I don't know exactly how much time had gone by, maybe it was half an hour, but the chief received a report. It's not that he personally received a report and it's not that he was in constant contact with them, but he heard this. He was following the communications. And at one point, it was said that Racak had been de-blocked and that conditions had been created for carrying out an on-site investigation. After that, the investigating judge got ready, deputy district public prosecutor Zivic too and Sasa Dobricanin, the pathologist; they got ready to conduct the on-site investigation. As far as I can remember, the assistant commander walked in, Zoran Djordjevic, and then the chief suggested to him that he should ensure a team to provide security, or rather, to prepare a group of policemen who would be the security detail for the on-site investigation team. As far as I can remember, General Djordjevic suggested to the chief of the secretariat to have one of the more senior police officers go along. And then the chief ordered me to go. He conveyed that to Djordjevic, assistant commander Djordjevic. He said, Get the people there and Mitic will go with the team for on-site investigation. That's the way it was roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me whether it is customary when an investigating judge comes and the entire team, is it usual practice for them to be escorted by a team that would accompany them, and is it usual that a police officer should come from the area where the investigating judge is coming to?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever an on-site investigation is to be carried out, police must be present to secure the location. At that time, due to the particular circumstances, I was ordered to go and take the team to Racak.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did the forensic team of the Urosevac SUP go to the on-site investigation on the 18th of January, 1999, in Racak?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember exactly all those people. Actually, I had worked with them in the secretariat. There was a chief of the division for combatting general crime, Rade Radovic; then Srecko Dogandzic, and Dragan Dabic, police officers, were there; and forensic technicians, Sasa Bozanic, and I believe the other was Sasa Andric.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You went to Racak with the investigative judge. Please tell us what was done once you got there.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we left for Racak which was soon after noon, we were in several vehicles. And I remember getting to the centre of the village where the investigative judge was stopped by police officer - I don't know who it was; there were two or three of them - and informed the judge that the bodies were in the mosque of Racak village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And what happened then?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigative judge and the team did their part of the work in the mosque. They took photographs of the bodies. They did everything they were supposed to do. And I must add that the OSCE Mission was also present. Because until the end of the on-site investigation, the OSCE Mission representatives were there. As far as I remember, there were three men and an Albanian girl who acted as an interpreter. Once they were done in the mosque and we were providing security to them, the investigative judge continued to the centre of the village, that is, to the location of the fighting. As far as I remember, lots of documents were found in the house, some pieces of uniforms, some pieces of weapons, and then we proceeded. I believe that there was also a bakery to bake bread for the terrorists. And there were some other facilities, food storages, and others. And then we went to the trenches that the Albanian terrorists had dug above the village. All around the village on the hill-side there were trenches, bunkers, and the like.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: When and how was the on-site investigation completed, and what happened?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that it was getting dark when the on-site investigation was being completed; I don't remember the exact hour. But throughout the time we were there, there was sporadic gun-fire. Bullets were flying. But in spite of that, the team completed their work. And on our way back, the on-site investigation team was driven by police officer. There was Danica Marinkovic, there was Dragomir Zivic, and the pathologist Sasa Dobricanin. They were in the vehicle that was right in front of mine. At one moment in time, we were being targeted, whether from a mortar or a hand-held rocket launcher, I'm in the sure, but there was a huge cloud of dust at one moment. And although the vehicle in which there was the judge and some other people was armoured, still a window pane cracked, but nobody got hurt.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did the KLA attack some buildings in Stimlje?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that on the 17th there was an attack on the special institute in Stimlje. A building in Stimlje was attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What did you do after the on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once everything had been completed, as far as I remember, we returned to Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see D150 now, and that is tab 37 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But before we start dealing with the document itself, let me ask you, sir, whether you know that -- know of any kidnappings during the burial of the persons killed in Racak; and if so, how did you learn about that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a significant number of persons of Albanian ethnicity were kidnapped. They had come to the burial and there was a crowd of people there. There were also armed members of the so-called KLA. They were also present at the burial. I remember that a significant number of people were kidnapped.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is a report of the staff of the MUP from Pristina. Do you know the two persons mentioned in paragraph one as being kidnapped? Who are they, what's their ethnicity, and what do they do, if you can provide that information?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember this case. It's about the Olluri family. These two persons were members of the reserve police forces. It says that Muhamed Olluri, age 28, and Rexhep Olluri, aged about 40, were kidnapped.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And in the last but one paragraph we see the name Zeqiri Hyseni?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Basri Zeqiri from Stimlje reported to the police station that Albanian terrorists had kidnapped his relative Hyseni Zeqiri.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know what these people were doing, and what was their attitude towards the authorities?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. Which persons?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The persons mentioned here. Do you know what they did?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't say anything about these persons. But I know that Hysen Olluri and Nazmi Olluri were members of the reserve police forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please see document D009-0937.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's tab 38 in your binder. It's a report on developments and activities dated 25 January, 1999. It's a report of the Urosevac SUP. To who was it sent?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report was sent to the staff of the MUP of Kosovo and Metohija in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And let us comment the last paragraph. Apart from the two -- first two paragraphs, tell us what the staff was informed about in the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here the staff was informed that in the coming period, that is, on the following day, it was planned to control the territory of the city of Urosevac from 1800 hours to 2400 hours by one department of the PJP.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were accounts of plans for the future an integral part of your reports that you submitted to the staff in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It says that the squad of the PJP of the MUP would control access to the city. Were these police officers who were performing regular duties in the Urosevac SUP?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This time around they were, but I don't know why this says that -- well, they are PJP members when they are engaged as such. These patrols were made up of these police officers due to their experience and their physical abilities, and that is why they are called PJP here. But otherwise, they are regular police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Are the activities they carry out here part of their regular duties in their organisational unit?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00829.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please see document 009 -- that is D009-0940.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It is dated the 29th of January, 1999, and it was sent to the MUP staff for AP KiM. It's a report on developments and activities. We again see some activities that have to do with the KVM. Was it your task to provide security to the KVM, and did you take steps to enable them to carry out the work that they were meant to do under the agreement?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. The OSCE Mission had diplomatic status, and we did everything necessary to provide adequate security to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you give them all information available to you that was of interest to them?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, always. We always provided information upon their request.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00830.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please see document D009-0912.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tab 40 in your binder, sir. This is a report on developments and activities of the Urosevac SUP dated the 1st of February, 1999. It was sent to the MUP staff. And what I'd like to know is whether you can give us any details about the incident mentioned in paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean on the 31st of January?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the period between 1800 and 2400 hours, the area of the town of Urosevac was checked --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, no, I mean the previous paragraph at about 2145.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 31st of January, 1999, at about 2145 hours, in the village of Gornje Godance, Stimlje municipality, three masked persons carried out a terrorist attack in the house of Xhevdet Zumeri, born in 1970. The attack was -- or rather, automatic weapons were used in the attack, and the following persons sustained serious injuries. Haljilj Boka, born in 1942; Bekim Duljaku, age 12; and Behrije Duljaku, age about 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, don't read any further, but tell us, were you informed of this event?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it, but I don't remember all the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This was sent to the MUP staff in Pristina. Was such a report sent to anybody else?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell, based on this description, but usually in case of such incidents, the operative centre and the crime police administration were usually informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So it was sent to all these?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00831.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D009-0947.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We now have a survey of developments dated the 4th of February of the Urosevac SUP. I would like to ask you about whether you are aware of this occurrence on the 4th of February, 1999, Witness?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is characteristic because I was actually there on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what your personal knowledge is?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After finding out, if I can put it that way, that the convoy with humanitarian aid had set out in the area of Jezerce and it had to go through the village of Gornje Nerodimlje, the villagers organised themselves, women, children, the elderly, adults, everybody went out into the centre of the road not allowing that humanitarian aid to go to the village of Jezerce. The locals reacted, asking the OSCE Mission to find, first of all, the two citizens from that village who had been kidnapped. As far as I can remember, Sinisa Lukic and Veselin Lazic. I know that village very well; my wife comes from that village. So I was sent by the chief of SUP with a number of policemen to make it possible for that humanitarian aid to get started because that was the order of the staff anyway. We went there. However, it was simply impossible to intervene under these circumstances because many people had gathered in one place. Finally, they insisted that the locals set up a delegation and inspect that humanitarian aid to make sure that no weapons were being provided to Albanian terrorists. Judging by the reaction of the citizens, there weren't any weapons at the time in the village of Jezerce when this check had been carried out. The members of the OSCE allowed that delegation from the village to inspect the trucks. That's when I cast a cursory glance and I saw that there were beds there, blankets, food, and other supplies. And then we managed to convince the locals. Ultimately we had to cordon off that convoy so that it could go to the village of Jezerce.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00832.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think it is time for the technical break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will adjourn now and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: ---Recess taken at 10.32 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could I please have D009-0950. Could we please have it on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tab 42 for you. This is a survey of incidents, occurrences, activities for the Urosevac SUP for the 5th of February, 1999. Who was it sent to?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the MUP staff for KiM in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We see here the incident that you talked about yesterday and a reference to the gratitude expressed by the members of the OSCE Verification Mission. And now, there's this section here where it says "they asked," can you see that part of the text, the last four lines? Could you please read it to yourself and explain.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We can barely hear the witness. Could both of his microphones be switched on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Humanitarian aid on that day was supposed to go where it was supposed to go.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The first part of the answer is missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We know that, but the question they inquired, et cetera, tell us about that.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Look at the next paragraph. "They inquired about ..." and then the last four lines.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, yes, I see. So when speaking to them, Mr. Jeff, if I remember that was his name, asked us whether they could establish contact with an Albanian family and an ethnic Serb family too, of course, that is to say, locals of the neighbouring Albanian villages, to have contact with them, and they wanted me to accompany them. I accepted gladly, and I remember that after that we went to an Albanian family.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Djurdjic. Could we go back to the bottom of the previous page in English, please. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00833.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D009-0953.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tab 43 for you. This is an Official Note of the Urosevac SUP dated the 7th of February, 1999. Radomir Mitic and Lecic, Milan signed it. Can you tell us about this Official Note in more detail? How did the situation develop?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, on the previous agreement reached with the members of the OSCE Mission, with went to the village of Donje Nerodimlje. I see that Lecic and I compiled this note about that. In addition to ourselves, Mr. Jeff and Marijana Cukic from Baranja were there. She was a university student, but she acted as an interpreter there. We went to pay a visit, and that's' when Mr. Jeff spoke to the the members of that family. You can see here what the content of the conversation was. I don't know what else you are interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would just like to know how come the interpreter reacted in this way, if you have a look at page 2, the third paragraph on page 2?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember that. Mr. Jeff went a bit ahead with Muharem Sejdiju, and I stopped a bit with interpreter and she told me on a one-on-one bases, now I'm going to quote what she said: You don't even need to bother about families like this because he is not interested. I was taken by surprise because I thought that he was interested in hearing from all the people of Kosovo, not literally all the people, but from all the structures of the people there to hear what the situation was like in Kosovo so that he wouldn't only be hearing from we from the police had to say. We don't want to be partial or anything. He was in a position there to hear what the situation was like from the citizens themselves, the locals.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00834.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D010-0791, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tab 44 for you. We have here a report with members of the OSCE. The document is signed by 2nd Lieutenant Radomir Mitic, who is our witness. Could you please tell us a bit more about the interest expressed by the KVM in persons who were brought in for interviews. Did they receive information, did they carry out checks, and was all of this made available to them?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I pointed out previously, the OSCE Mission had all information made available and accessible to them, so in this case as well. I made every effort to familiarise them with all facts and circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please give us your comment concerning what is at the end of this report, special observations or remarks?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that. This is exactly what she said to me as I quoted it here: "Good-bye Mr. Mitic, I hope we meet again, unless they bomb you, in which case we will all be moving out already tomorrow."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did draw any conclusions on that basis?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My situation was that they were abreast of the situation, that they had the situation under control, and that NATO bombing was inevitable.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00835.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 4103. That's from the Prosecutors's 65 ter list. 0413, sorry, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's tab 45 for you. This is a dispatch of the Urosevac SUP dated the 20th [as interpreted] of February, 1999. Can you tell us what your comments would be with regard to the incident referred to here, the one that occurred on the 28th of February, 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a dispatch of the Urosevac SUP sent to the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, to the UKP, that is to say, the administration of crime police, the the operation centre, and the police administration in Belgrade, and to the MUP staff for the Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija in Pristina. I remember what happened. The chief of the secretariat came to know that a person by the name of Riza Kiki had been kidnapped on that day. And he sent the commander of the police station of Kacanik, and with a group of policemen they were supposed to go to the village of Ivaja or rather, Gajre. Actually, they were sent to Ivaja, but Riza Kiki is from Gajre. Sorry about that. They sent them there to check this information. When they entered the village, terrorists opened fire, heavy fire at that, and the chief of police from Kacanik lost his life and four policemen were seriously wounded. The OSCE Mission, as I was informed then by the chief, had been notified so that they could follow the police. However, they had refused to come with the police. After the death of the commander and the wounding of these four policemen, they did show up eventually, because I was in Kacanik too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00836.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have D008-5655.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is a statement of Brava, Sehat, and the date is the 3rd of March, 1999. He gave it to the employees of the crime police administration in Urosevac. Witness, do you know what the situation was like in the month of March in the part of the municipality of Kacanik that bordered on the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, we had intelligence at the time - I dare call it concrete intelligence - from our sources, locals and others, that in the area around Ivaja, Kotlina, Pustenik, and I believe Gorance was the name of the village on the border of Macedonia, that all around these villages strong terrorist forces were gathering and that they were receiving weapons from the direction of Tetovo in Macedonia. That is, that they were arming themselves at a massive scale, that they were mobilising people by force, and training there. Which meant that they were planning on conducting a fierce attack on the military and everybody who was to be found in or about the Kacanik gorge.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00837.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see D010-0794, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That is tab 47 in your binder, sir. This is a letter from the SUP of Urosevac dated the 3rd of March, 1999, sent to the staff of the MUP for KiM to Lieutenant-Colonel Dusko Adamovic. Can you say -- can you give us any details about the contents and the subject of this letter?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that the chief of the secretariat had this information. Actually, that's what I remember, more or less, because he hailed from the area of Strbac. He probably reserved information from our positions or the locals that a laser beam was directed from Brezovica by two unidentified persons. However, the incident was not reported in a timely fashion so that no measures were taken. I don't understand this --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, there is also item 2 here, and this report -- what does this report treat or deal with? What kind of problems? How did your SUP react to that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again there was a problem in the village of Gornje Nerodimlje, that was the second such instance. The first time around, I explained how we resolved the problem, but the locals were sore because the OSCE Mission members did nothing about the people who were abducted from that village. So that they didn't allow convoys with humanitarian aid to pass through.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Does this refer to the families of the persons who were kidnapped?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Actually, it was practically all the population of those -- of that village who had gathered, and the fiercest reaction was that of the son of the kidnapped Veselin Lazic. He was even in poor health, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you inform the staff of the MUP in Pristina about problems related to the safety of the KVM?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, regularly. Whenever necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you cover up any such problems?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. There was no need to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00838.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please see document D010-0796.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's tab 48, sir. This is a list of incidents of the Urosevac SUP dated the 8th of March, 1999. To who was it sent, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was sent to the staff of the MUP for AP KiM in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Here we see in the fourth and fifth paragraphs that the KVM were interested in the apprehension of persons and their being interviewed. Did you give them information about that and state the reasons for these interviews?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We gave them the relevant information about everything they were interested in. I remember when they came to see me personally, I couldn't always give them a firsthand answer, but through the chief of the OKP or through other channels, I checked the information and then gave it to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00839.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see D008-0687.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's tab 99 [as interpreted]. This is the statement of Beqa Shefqet which he gave to members of the OKP Urosevac on the 10th of March, 1999. I'm interested in the information that you had of the activities of the KLA at the time in and around Dubrava village?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can repeat that the villages of Gajre, Ivaja, Kotlina, Pustenik, Gorance were in the area where strong forces of the so-called KLA were concentrated. They were well armed, and they were constantly mobilising people forcibly. We had intelligence to that effect, so their numbers grew constantly. And in accordance with our operative intelligence, they were meant to be the logistics for NATO's entry into the FRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was there any reaction of the SUP, a reaction to the KLA attacks directed against civilian population?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can claim that with full responsibility. Based on everything I know, there has never been any activity taken against the civilian population or the Albanian ethnic group, only against terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00840.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please see document D009-0905. And that's tab 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We have in front of us a report on developments and activities of the Urosevac SUP dated 12 March, 1999. To whom was it sent?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report was sent to the MUP staff for the Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please comment paragraph 1 of this report for us.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Report on developments and activities --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, you don't have to read it out aloud. Just give me your -- what -- give me what you know about the events mentioned in paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at that time, indeed, we had intelligence to the effect that individual members of the OSCE Mission are grouping and marking bridges in the area around Strbac. I remember that they -- I remember receiving information from the Strpce police station that they had noticed such activities of members of the OSCE Mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm now interested in paragraph 5. What information did you have on the 12th of March, 1999? Could you please comment.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember this case. There was a military column, and it so happened that a police patrol was patrolling the road at the same time. Then both the army and the police were attacked. Fire was opened at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, the following paragraph, can you comment and share with us any information you have about that and similar such incidents?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that attack, certain persons were brought in for purpose of information. Their names are mentioned. And it was in the area of the villages I mentioned. This is the road from Urosevac to Doganovic and further on to the border crossing of Globocica. And on that section of the road from Doganovic to Globocica, the attack took place. The operation was continued to apprehend the terrorists, that is, those who had carried out the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00841.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you know that in March attacks on the army and the police as well as on vehicles moving on the road from Stimlje to Dulje were continued?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were frequent attacks. Actually, they hardly ever stopped from 1998 on. The attacks took place almost daily, and there were real problems there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see document D009-0919.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's tab 52 in your binder. This is a letter from the SUP of Urosevac dated the 14th of March, 1999. To whom was it sent?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was sent to the staff of the MUP for the AP KiM in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please comment the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's about an attack on members of the military, that is, a vehicle of the military. Soldier Aleksandar Mladenovic was lightly injured. I know that the traffic police provided first aid and that he was taken to an infirmary.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00842.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please see the 65 ter document of the Prosecution 01243.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's tab 53 in your binder, sir. Witness, what we have before us is a survey of events, occurrences, and activities of the SUP Urosevac on the 15th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This dispatch, or rather, document, were sent to the staff of the MUP for Kosovo and Metohija in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I would just like you to give us your comments on the last paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, I'm not objecting, but I can't find the document. I'm wondering if it's on one of the lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document is right before you. My learned friend, it is your 65 ter number 01243, and on the basis of that number, we had this document called up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djurdjic. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you see that third paragraph?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What is it that the verifiers were asking about here?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They inquired about the persons who had been brought into custody.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: On which day were these persons brought into custody?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were brought in on the 12th of March, 1999. And the question was what would be his fate and how long he would stay at the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the document of the 12th of March, the survey of events, again, that there was that list of a number of persons who were brought in for interviews?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I remember that from the previous document. It was roughly those persons. Now, most of these persons were released and some were detained for further processing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We see here that all these persons were released except for the two names mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I would be interested in the following now: How did the members of the KVM obtain the names of persons who were brought in for interviews, and how did they know about that in the first place?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can just make an assumption; I cannot make an assertion. But it's most probable that the families of those persons contacted the KVM, so it was under that pressure as it were that they came to check it out with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00843.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D007-0116.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It is tab 54 for you. We have before us an Official Note of the Kacanik police station compiled on the 16th of March, 1999. And I would be interested in the following: What is your knowledge, what information did you have with regard to the very last part of this Official Note? So after what was stated in this Official Note.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I understand things, or actually, let me say first of all that the deputy commander of the police station of Kacanik filed this Official Note, and I see my own handwriting in the upper right-hand corner that I initialled it for the state security department and for the crime police department, in the upper right-hand corner. This has to do with the following information: Mr. Sulejman Loku came and stated that a group of armed men came on the 27th of February, 1999, with KLA insignia and they took away his hunting rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I actually asked you about the very last part, the last two or three sentences.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here in the note that they actually expelled them into the forest. They didn't allow them to move out of there until the police arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you have any intelligence to the effect that the KLA was relocating the population from their villages?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. In several places we obtained this kind of intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.
