utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00844.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D008-5437, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's number 55 for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D008-5637.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you something before that, Witness. We have here Rafiz Lika's statement that he gave to the OKP of Urosevac on the 20th of March. I would like to ask you about the mobilisation carried out by the KLA in the areas towards the Macedonian border in March 1999.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, members of the so-called KLA carried out forest mobilisation in addition to their other activities. They threatened people, intimidated them, they resorted to all sorts of methods in order to have as many people as possible in their ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00845.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, we had several documents here related to KLA activities in the part of the Kacanik municipality facing the Macedonian border. Were there any reactions to such KLA terrorist activity in March 1999? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that, according to the same principle, the chief of secretariat compiled a proposal and sent it to the staff, namely to arrest terrorists in Ivaja, Kotlina, Pustenik, in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether this action was actually carried out?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that this action was carried out. Now, I know for sure that the Urosevac company of the PJP took part. I am not sure, but I think it was also the PJP of the Gnjilane SUP and members of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This action was aimed against who?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only this action, but all actions were aimed against Albanian terrorists. By no means were they aimed against civilians, Albanians as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: After this action, was an on-site investigation carried out?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember, and I think I actually saw Ms. Milicevic, Ljiljana I think her first name was. She was the municipal investigating judge. And also Boza Radic, the municipal public prosecutor in Urosevac. They carried out the on-site investigation together with the team from Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D002-4416.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, what about the forensic team from the Urosevac SUP, did they compile their report?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see that here. The forensic team wrote up a report on that on-site investigation too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know what was found in these villages?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, a certain amount of weapons were found, but truth to tell, I do not remember the exact amount. Then parts of uniform -- also there were some bunkers in the area where terrorists had been hiding and from where they attacked the army and the police. I think that's the way it was then.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D002-4424.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Are these photographs of these bunkers in the forest, Witness?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes those are the bunkers that were in the forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we also have D002-4423 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: These are photographs that show what was found on the scene. We see the victims and we see the equipment.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is this all one document, Mr. Djurdjic? I believe the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, certainly, because the photographs were not translated, naturally. It's only the text that was translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00846.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have document D008-5649.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's tab 57 for you. We have here a statement that was given to the Urosevac OKP on the 26th of March, 1999. The statement was made by Laqi, Naser?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, after this action, people were brought in, people who were taking part in terrorist activities. Was this done by your policemen?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, regular policemen were involved only in bringing these persons in. In the field, it's probably the PJPs and the military that came across these persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And then these interviews were conducted. We have a statement here, and to the best of your knowledge, was that information corroborated about the activities of the KLA in Ivaja and Kotlina in March?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was confirmed. What was found was what I described a few moments ago; equipment, weapons, fortifications, trenches, dugouts, et cetera, bunkers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00847.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D008-5631, could we have that document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It is tab 58 for you. Witness, we have a statement here of Loki, Kadri on the 6th of April, 1999. He gave it to the OKP of the Urosevac SUP. Can you please give us your comments with regard to paragraph 2 and your knowledge at the time about the area that we are talking about and also what the situation was like during the course of the war.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, we knew all the things that I've already spoken about, so we had all that intelligence, and this person indeed confirmed that strong forces of the terrorist gangs were concentrated in that area, that they were carrying out forced mobilisation, and that they were making efforts to take steps in order to act as the infantry that would allow a NATO land invasion of the FRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00848.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see D008-5635.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's tab 60. We'll see a statement dated the 14th of April, 1999. It was is a statement taken from Elezi, Dufki [as interpreted] by the OKP about the same area. Does this confirm the information that you had at the time?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statement of Rufki Elezi indeed confirms all information that we had previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00849.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see D006-4596.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's tab 59 in your binder. We can see a criminal report of the OKP of the Urosevac SUP dated the 25th of April, 1999, about events that took place on the 8th of April, 1999, at an entry point to the town of Kacanik. What do you know about this event, and can you give us more details?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember this event perfectly well. I remember that there was a police patrol on the road toward the border crossing of Djeneral Jankovic. That area was constantly targeted by terrorists. At the -- in the outskirts of Kacanik, I think that was the Duskaja settlement, across the road from the gas station, there was a newly built housing development. And, from that area, strong fire was opened at the Pinzgauer vehicle. I haven't had a chance to read this, but I believe that eight police officers were wounded then.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In all these incidents, or rather, after all these incidents, did forensic technicians go to the locations to carry out an on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't possible to do that immediately in this case. And then upon the instructions given by the chief of SUP, patrols were sent out to provide assistance and conduct a search for the terrorists. After the operation which went on until the following day, so after the end of the operation, the on-site investigation was carried out, photographs were taken, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see page 5 of the English version and page 006-4599 of the Serbian version. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What is this?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In your binder it is under number 623. Go back. This must be it. It reads "Case File Cover." Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And now the following page, please. In the lower corner you can see number 624?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is the report of the forensic technicians?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's about an on-site investigation conducted on the 9th of April, 1995 [as interpreted], and drawn up on the 21st of May of the same year.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go to the following page, please. Could we please see pages 8 and 9 of the English version. In line 4, page 51, should read 1999 rather than 1995. I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm told it's over 130 pages, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm tendering just the one that I showed. The English translation also contains images. So I'm just tendering the documents that I referred to. The English pages are the ones that I showed, that is, the criminal report, and forensic examination report, and the pages that were displayed. I just want to tender these.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will try to identify and separate those, and they will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00850.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see Exhibit P1205.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In your binder, it is tab 61. This is a dispatch of the department of public security dated 15 January 1999, signed by General Vlastimir Djordjevic, chief of the RJB. Tell us to which SUPs was this dispatch sent?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was sent to all SUPs in the Republic of Serbia from 1 til 33.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you receive this dispatch in the Urosevac SUP?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the chief did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with its contents?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after the reception of this dispatch, the chief gave out tasks to the individual departments and tasked the heads of department to act in accordance with the dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see Exhibit P356.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tab 62 in your binder. This is dispatch number 312 of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia dated the 18th of February, 1999. That is, it was sent out by the assistant minister and the chief of the department of public security General Vlastimir Djordjevic. Can you tell us to which SUPs this dispatch was sent?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was sent to all SUPs in the Republic of Serbia, the chief from item 1 til item 33.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you receive this dispatch at the Urosevac SUP?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We received it through the chief, and he informed us of its contents.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What was the security situation like at the time, and which measures were supposed to take in a -- pursuant to this dispatch, or which measures did you take?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We acted in accordance with the instructions contained in this dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We can see item 1 here?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, update the defence plan. That's what we did. An officer was charged with monitoring these activities. This refers to updating of lists, mobilisation, and the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Under item 4, were there any tasks for your department?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. We had some untrained staff, so we had to train them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And did you act in accordance with items 5 and 6?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Item 5, yes, item 6 also.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In the introduction on page 1 of this dispatch, it's pointed out that there's a realistic threat of the FRY being attacked by NATO. Did you have information about the situation at the time when this dispatch arrived at the SUP of Urosevac and everywhere else?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is well known that the situation in Kosovo and Metohija was very difficult at the time. And as for the NATO bombing, well, we were informed because we had -- we followed the media coverage.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see Exhibit D438.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is dispatch dated the 2nd of March, 1999. It is a dispatch of the -- of Vlastimir Djordjevic. To which SUPs was it sent?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to dispatch 433? It was sent to all SUPs in the Republic of Serbia from items 1 -- from item 1 to item 33, to the chief, to the staff in Pristina, and to the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And what were you instructed to do by this dispatch, and did you implement that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was passive-duty service introduced from 2200 hours til 700 hours, and only in exceptional cases, if there are good reasons, should policemen be allowed to take leave.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat what he just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see P1206, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is dispatch number 597, dated the 22nd of March, 1999. It's a dispatch of the assistant minister and chief of the public security department Colonel-General Vlastimir Djordjevic. To which SUPs was it sent?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To all SUPs in the Republic of Serbia from 1 to 33, to the chief, the staff of the MUP in Pristina, and the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What were you instructed to do by this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were instructed to intensify the measures as laid out in the previous dispatch, as far as I can tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And these dispatches were sent out whenever there was a threat of war?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And two or three dispatches with similar contents are mentioned here; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Number 312 of 18 February; 1685 of 18 September; and 1827 of 7 October; as well as the last number, 451 of 8 October 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please see document D -- sorry, it's Exhibit D248.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We see in front of us an order of the staff of the MUP in Pristina dated 26 March 1999. To who was this dispatch sent?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To all SUPs in Kosovo and Metohija, to the chief, and every -- it went to the commands of every detachment of the PJP.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you act in accordance with this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This was the 26th of March. The war had already started in 1999; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see Exhibit D253.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's tab 66 in your binder. This is a dispatch of the chief of the department of public security dated 27th March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, to who was this dispatch sent? To which SUPs, that is.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To all SUPs from item 1 to item 33 and to the chiefs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What did you do pursuant to this dispatch, and why was it sent out?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I understand, this dispatch was sent out because measures should be taken to find locators affixed to certain buildings or facilities that could be used for the purpose of bombing by NATO.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you find any such devices in the territory of Urosevac?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I remember we did, but I don't remember the exact locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you act in accordance with this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see Exhibit D249, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's 67 in your binder. This is a dispatch of the MUP staff in Pristina dated the 2nd of April, 1999. Could you please tell us who it was sent to, this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This dispatch was sent to all chiefs of SUP in the area of Kosovo and Metohija and commanders of PJP detachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would you you please tell me, in relation to paragraphs 1, 2, and 3, did you act accordingly?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We acted in accordance with this dispatch and previous ones, however, specifically on the basis of this dispatch, we established joint patrols. These patrols actually had the task to do the following: Since they were mixed patrols consisting of members of the military and the police, they were supposed to curb crime among members of the military and police, and the citizens too, of course, but primarily within the ranks of the military and the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have document P47.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's tab 69 for you. We have here a decree on Internal Affairs during a state of war. Witness, I think that we already discussed this subject a bit, a change in disciplinary proceedings in a state of war from the time when had this decree was passed. Could you please tell me what happened in practice. How was this decree amended?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before this decree was passed, disciplinary proceedings took place in a regular fashion. There was a disciplinary prosecutor, a disciplinary chamber or court, and a disciplinary investigator, if it had to do with a crime. If a member of the police or the secretariat had committed a crime. According to this decree, the proceedings are shortened. The head of the organisational unit to which the policeman or employee who was the perpetrator belonged collects all information with regard to that and submits a proposal to the chief of secretariat who then decides on the disciplinary measure that is to be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the very last subparagraph of Article 9, it says that "the prescribed measures and punishments for serious violations of professional duties and responsibility shall be pronounced by the head of a sector of the ministry or a person authorised by him"?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. The chief of secretariat in my secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have P1050.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tab 70 for you. We have here a document dated the 9th of April, 1999, and it was sent by the public security department to ... could you please tell us?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was sent to all secretariats of the interior of the Republic of Serbia, to all the chiefs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, we have all the rest. Tell me, if we look at this document, the introductory part, what is the head of public security saying to all these addressees?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition to serious violations of work duty --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, no, just the first two paragraphs. That's what I'm asking about.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, the first two paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What did he make you aware of?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Official Gazette of the Republic of Serbia, is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did he make you aware of the changes that took place?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, on page 2, the chief of the public security sector --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, authorised the chiefs of SUPs. Specifically in my situation it was the chief of the secretariat who had the right to impose disciplinary measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have D262, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's tab 71 in your binder. The 21st of April, 1999, is the date, and it was sent by Petar Zekovic, General Petar Zekovic. Did you receive this?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So what is stated here?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The assistant minister, Major-General Petar Zekovic, explains in greater detail what the procedure should be in case of disciplinary proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And who was this sent to?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was sent to all chiefs of secretariat SUPs in the territory of the Republic of Serbia and other organisational units as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that this would be the time for the technical break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, we will have the second break now. We resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Can we now please see Exhibit P1207.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tab 72 in your binder. This is a dispatch of the chief of the department of public security General Vlastimir Djordjevic dated the 12th of April, 1999. Kindly tell us to which SUPs it was sent.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To all SUPs in the Republic of Serbia, that is, the chiefs of the SUPs from 1 to 33.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In item 1, what is dealt with, and what is to be done?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says in co-operation with the town and municipal civil protection staffs and others, monitoring and finding locators is ordered.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were there obligations under item 3 also?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We were obliged to act under item 3 also.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were you acquainted with the dispatch once it arrived at the Urosevac SUP?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the chief of the secretariat acquainted us with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see D004-1916.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That is tab 73 in your binder. It's a dispatch of the MUP staff for KiM dated the 29 of April, 1999. Can you tell us to who it was sent?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To all SUPs in Kosovo and Metohija, the chiefs of the SUPs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were you familiarised with the dispatch when it arrived?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Which measures did you take pursuant to this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All measures were taken for police forces to behave in accordance with the dispatch in the course of carrying out their jobs and their tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It is mentioned here what is to be used. Was that really used?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were mostly helmets and protective jackets.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00851.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see Exhibit D254.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That is tab 74 in your binder. This is a dispatch of the chief of the public security department of the MUP of Serbia. Can you tell us to which SUPs it was sent?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This dispatch was sent to all SUPs in the Republic of Serbia and the staff of the MUP in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you act in accordance with this dispatch, and which measures did you take? To what activities does this dispatch refer?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The dispatch applied practically to all staff of the ministry and its organisational units. We acted in accordance with the instructions in the dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see Exhibit D443.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tab 75 in your binder. Witness, this dispatch is a dispatch of the staff of the MUP in Pristina dated 6 May 1999. To who was this dispatch sent?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To all secretariats in Kosovo and Metohija and the commanders of the -- of PJPs 21 through 87 as well as to the special anti-terrorist unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What did you do pursuant to paragraph 1 of this letter?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All police staff were acquainted with the contents as laid out in paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What exactly was that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an -- it's the reports of the president of the FRY by the head of the MUP Major-General Sreten Lukic and the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What about the other organisational units?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The organisational units informed their respective staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: To who did they -- you forward this exactly?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the police stations outside the SUP headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please see document D004-1619.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is a dispatch of the MUP staff of the Republic of Serbia in Pristina dated 2 June 1999. Tell us to who it was sent.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To all SUPs in Kosovo and Metohija, that is, the chiefs and to the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you act pursuant to this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00852.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, when the bombing and the war started, were there movements of the population?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of the war, that is, the NATO aggression on the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, from the area covered by the secretariat for which I worked, there were citizens of all ethnicities leaving; that is, Albanians, Serbs, Roma, and others. And I too relocated my family to Serbia proper, to Pozarevac, that is, our children. There was a work obligation in place for us. I worked with the police, and my wife worked at the post office. Of course, not the entire population was leaving but great numbers were going in all directions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: After the beginning of the bombing, did the population from the surrounding rural areas come to Urosevac?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. From the villages around Urosevac where anti-terrorist activities had taken place or where there had been fighting between the police and the so-called KLA, from those areas, and from other villages where even cluster bombs were dropped. People were leaving those places because they were scared, and came to town.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You mentioned cluster bombs being dropped. Do you have firsthand knowledge about such bombs?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know several locations where cluster bombs were dropped. I know for sure that the Simporex [phoen] factory was targeted. That is along the road from Urosevac to Skopje or Urosevac Strpce. I don't know how many exactly were dropped there, but it was certainly a huge amount that were dropped in that area. According to the information that we had - it must have been in Duganovic Selo or Dubrava, certainly thereabouts - cluster bombs were dropped, and, as far as I remember, two or three children of Albanian ethnicity played with that bomb and lost their lives in the process. In the area of Gornje Nerodimlje, there was also a massive drop of cluster bombs. As far as I remember, on the hill above Stimlje too, in the village of Kostanje, cluster bombs were dropped. One soldier was lethally injured and four were seriously wounded. There may have been more locations, but I'm sure about these. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: During the bombing, was there an inflow of people to Urosevac who later left the town?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, there's a railroad station in Urosevac, and that railroad station -- or rather, there's a railroad line from Kosovo Polje through Urosevac and it goes on to Skopje, and there were trains running through Urosevac, I don't know whether they were regular or special lines, but there were people on those trains.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you have any contact with the people who were leaving Urosevac?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember one such instance. I think it was after the bombing of the column that was moving toward Djakovica. A large number of people gathered at the train station if Urosevac. And I received instructions from the chief of the SUP to go there and warn those people to leave the place because they were likely to be the target of a NATO attack. I knew some of these people. I had seen them before and had tried to persuade them to return to their homes because they really could become the target of an attack. But they said to me, We are already leaving and there's no going back. So they didn't heed my warnings. They said that the reason for the departure was the NATO bombing. Whether there was another reason, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did the people leave Urosevac by other means of transportation too?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did. The town of Urosevac -- or rather, not many people left the town of Urosevac because throughout the war we met each other and had in contact. I even saw Albanians and Serbs sitting in cafes together and having coffees -- or having coffee or anything else to drink.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did the Urosevac SUP or any other body of the MUP organise transportation for Albanians to leave the town?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the Urosevac SUP never did that. I can tell you firsthand that I went to talk to those people and persuade them to return to their homes, but I couldn't force anyone to do that because the law didn't allow me to. But I know for sure that nobody from the SUP organised transportation. Whatever was organised, whether there were buses or trains, well, that was organised on a private basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you take measures against certain organisations that violated the rules about the transportation of persons?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I know, we filed some criminal reports. Actually, the officers from the crime police department did because there were complaints by citizens - and we also had intelligence to that effect - that on buses they were charging much more money than the official price of the ticket. So that several persons were detained because of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: During the war in 1999, in accordance with the laws and regulations in force in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, were all persons leaving the country obliged to pay an exit tax?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All citizens of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia were obliged to pay such a tax upon leaving the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you take any measures about that, and were there perhaps instances of officials abusing their position at the border itself, overcharging those on the way out?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were several instances of that happening, and I do remember that some persons were actually prosecuted for doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if at any point in time throughout 1998 or 1999 you ever issued instructions for measures to be taken against Albanian civilians for their expulsion or for any form of abuse of the Albanians to be tolerated or indeed for efforts to displace them to be encouraged?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I've never done anything like that. Even in cases -- or rather, had I found out that any of my subordinates engaged in that type of activity, I would have taken steps, disciplinary steps, specifically against those persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What about your police officers. Did they, in fact, escort any Albanians leaving the country to Albania or Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no information indicating that any of the police were involved in escorting those columns.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness. This concludes my examination-in-chief. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We have about one or two minutes, Mr. Stamp. Would you think it more reasonable to commence tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I certainly would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we should then adjourn to resume tomorrow at 9 a.m. We must adjourn now, the courtroom is used for another trial, and we continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. A Court Officer will assist you after we rise. Thank you.
